2. Learned counsel for the petitioner states
body: that the law favours all matters to be decided on merits instead of dismissal on technical grounds and as the counsel for the petitioner had proceeded to another city in connection with some other case and could not reach back within time due to circumstances beyond control, hence prays that in the interest of justice another opportunity may be granted to the petitioner to crossexamine witnesses of the respondents.

3. On the other hand the learned counsel for respondents No. 1 to 4 has controverted arguments of the counsel for the petitioner and defended the impugned orders and prays for dismissal of the instant petition.

4. The claim of the petitioner that sufficient opportunity was not provided to her before passing the impugned order dated 25.07.2024, whereby her right to cross-examine the PWs has been struck off, is based on the facts that on the fateful day, her counsel appeared in the court in the earlier part of the day and informed the court that he had to proceed to Kasur in connection with another matter and would cross-examine the witness of the other side on his return to Lahore but he was late in reaching the court and in the meanwhile petitioner’s right was struck off and claims that petitioner is ready to do the needful, for which purpose prays that a single opportunity be provided to her, which request is opposed by the learned counsel for the respondents on the ground that the petitioner was avoiding to proceed with the trial of the suit just to delay the matter for an indefinite time with mala fide intentions.

5. As the plea has been raised by the petitioner that she could not cross-examine the witnesses of the respondents as the learned counsel representing her appeared in the court in the earlier part of the day and informed the court that he was to proceed to Kasur in connection with some other cases and would crossexamine the witnesses on his return, which could not be done and today the learned counsel states at the bar that he returned late on the said date due to circumstances beyond his control, which in the absence of any contrary material available on record is taken as correct on the touchstone of well settled traditions and norms of legal profession as held in the judgment reported as Muhammad Fayyaz and another versus Returning Officer, Union Council No.20, Lodhran and 4 others (2006 YLR 797 Lahore). Hence without further commenting upon the merits of the case in detail, while relying upon the principles laid down in judgment reported as Zahoor Ahmed vs. Mehra through Legal Heirs and others (1999 SCMR 105), it is observed that instead of deciding the matter on technical grounds, it would be appropriate and in the interest of justice to provide one opportunity to the petitioner to cross-examine the PWs subject to payment of costs of Rs. 20,000/-, which shall be paid to the other party before the trial court on production of certified copy of this order, whereafter the said court shall fix a date when the petitioner shall cross-examine the PWs and join further proceedings in the matter. In case of failure on the part of the petitioner to do the needful, the trial court will be at liberty to proceed further with the matter in accordance with law. The petition is allowed in the foregoing terms.
